title: Finite-stage detection of alteration objects and prime-to-ell generic degrees
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_a)_{a\in I}$ an inverse system of reduced affine Noetherian schemes with affine etale transition maps [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume every $S_a$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], and that the inverse limit $S$ is reduced Noetherian. Fix $a_0\in I$ and a prime $\ell$ invertible on $S_{a_0}$. Let finitely many schemes $V_{b,a_0}$ of finite presentation over $S_{a_0}$, and finitely many morphisms between them, be given [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $V_{b,a}=V_{b,a_0}\times_{S_{a_0}}S_a$ and $V_b=V_{b,a_0}\times_{S_{a_0}}S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If every $V_b\to S$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, then there exists $a_1\geq a_0$ such that every $V_{b,a}\to S_a$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S_a$ for all $a\geq a_1$. Here the objects and maximally $\ell'$-finite morphisms are exactly those of [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]: reduced finite-type sources, all component generic points mapping to component generic points with finite residue-field extensions [def-weil-residue-field]. If any of the specified morphisms $V_b\to V_c$ are maximally $\ell'$-finite, $a_1$ may also be chosen so that all their models are maximally $\ell'$-finite for every $a\geq a_1$. Empty objects are permitted. No properness, surjectivity, covering-family, regularity, or boundary conclusion is included.

source.place: Expose III Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, printed pp.43--44, generic-degree and alteration-object permanence in its etale limit argument; compare III Proposition 3.1(i) and its finite-free generic-rank model argument, pp.37--38. Agent-formulated finite-stage interface for etale inverse systems, not the approximation-by-congruent-sections assertion of III 3.1. Finite-presentation descent is Stacks limits.tex Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation); ind-etale residue fields are separable algebraic (algebraic field-factorizations and their finite ranks descend to a finite stage).
